why: monthly run: this month's jobs report (2026-10-02) and CPI (2026-10-14) are both out
key_risks: 10-year Treasury yields breaking sustainably above 5.25% would trigger multiple compression across high-duration growth sectors and tighten borrowing conditions.
10y at 5.10% and a hawkish Oct 27-28 FOMC pressuring valuations; HY spreads already widening to 3.23.

CALC:pullback_risk (p=0.074, oos_auc only 0.68 — the weakest model in the packet) is based on Baa spreads and realized vol, both still calm (VIX 16.46, 42nd pctile), but it doesn't capture the 96th-percentile Geopolitical Risk Index, 94th-percentile EPU, or 84th-percentile oil volatility (OVX 49.1) — all flashing risk that a low-vol equity tape is currently ignoring.

CALC:recession_risk (p_12m=0.094, oos_auc=0.873) is low and driven mainly by loose NFCI and a positive yield curve, but it does not directly model an active, compounding supply shock (Hormuz exports -40%, diesel +70% YoY, Brent 97th percentile) that could squeeze corporate margins and consumer spending power faster than its financial-conditions-based drivers would pick up.

Ceasefire collapse in the Russia-Ukraine energy war (NOTE:E11/E12) and continuing Hormuz tanker attacks (NOTE:E1/E4) raise the odds of a further oil/diesel spike that a model calibrated on 5-year history (DCOILBRENTEU z=+2.5) may underweight as an outlier.
Geopolitical escalation widens oil volatility beyond current price

Headline CPI reacceleration (3.72%) risks a sentiment/political reaction even though core inflation (2.57%) is stable; a misreading of this as broad-based inflation could trigger a more hawkish Fed repricing than our modest +10bp rates call assumes.
Hormuz/Gulf escalation removing more supply (Brent already $126.55, OVX 49) while the pullback model misses geopolitics.
Low saving rate (4.1) and sentiment (51.7) with $4.33 gasoline and $6.33 diesel could crack consumer spending.
Payrolls remain below 50k triggering policy shift
Prolonged closure or worsening naval attacks in the Strait of Hormuz could push crude above $140/bbl, driving headline inflation well above 4.5% and causing broad consumer retrenchment.
Statistical pullback risk is estimated at 7.4%, but a rapid flare-up in geopolitical tensions could spike VIX from 16.46 and widen HY credit spreads rapidly from 3.23%.
Upside risk: ceasefire or de-escalation triggers a sharp oil reversal toward EIA $105.
